pr.body:
Changes:
- Initializes unified storage when the `ResourceServer` is created, instead of doing it inside the first gRPC call it receives. This was causing context cancelled errors since the index takes too long to build within the context of the gRPC call.
- Fixes trace propagation by passing span contexts down.
- Improves index build speed using finer grain locking when writing the index cache. We were locking the whole `BuildIndex` function, which was slowing things down when building many namespaces with high concurrency.

Notes for reviewer:
- Does anything else depend on initializing US lazily? What could this break?
pr.title: Unified Storage: Init at startup, fix traces, and speed up indexing

raw_findings.body: The check-then-build sequence is no longer serialized. For file-backed indexes (size > FileThreshold) both goroutines call bleve.New on the same directory; the second call fails with an index-already-exists error, returning an error to the search request. For memory indexes, two full builds run and one index is silently overwritten in the cache, wasting work and leaking the loser index.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Concurrent searches on an uncached namespace/resource intermittently fail with a bleve index-creation error or perform duplicate index builds.
raw_findings.impact: The check-then-build sequence is no longer serialized. For file-backed indexes (size > FileThreshold) both goroutines call bleve.New on the same directory; the second call fails with an index-already-exists error, returning an error to the search request. For memory indexes, two full builds run and one index is silently overwritten in the cache, wasting work and leaking the loser index.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch removed the coarse lock that made the GetIndex-nil check and BuildIndex atomic, without adding any per-key serialization to replace it.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add per-key build synchronization (e.g., singleflight or a per-key mutex) so concurrent callers for the same key wait for one build, while different keys can still build in parallel.
raw_findings.title: Removing BuildIndex-wide lock allows concurrent duplicate builds of the same index
raw_findings.trigger: Two concurrent Search (or handleEvent) calls hit searchSupport.getOrCreateIndex for the same NamespacedResource whose index is not yet cached; both see GetIndex return nil and both invoke BuildIndex simultaneously.

raw_findings.body: Concurrent map read and map write on bleveBackend.cache is a fatal runtime error in Go, crashing the storage server during startup; even when it does not crash, the count read is racy.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Intermittent 'concurrent map read and map write' fatal panic during search index initialization on busy instances.
raw_findings.impact: Concurrent map read and map write on bleveBackend.cache is a fatal runtime error in Go, crashing the storage server during startup; even when it does not crash, the count read is racy.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch adds a TotalDocs() call at a point where the newly started event-handling goroutine can concurrently mutate the same unlocked cache map.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Acquire cacheMu.RLock inside bleveBackend.TotalDocs (or move this log line before the watch goroutine is started).
raw_findings.title: New TotalDocs() call reads bleve cache map without lock while event handler can build indexes concurrently
raw_findings.trigger: The watch-event goroutine started a few lines earlier (go func { ... s.handleEvent(...) }) processes a pending write event for an uncached resource and triggers a BuildIndex (map write under cacheMu) at the same moment this new log line iterates bleveBackend.cache via TotalDocs, which takes no lock.

raw_findings.body: The only integration test exercising the storage-server module target now runs on neither sqlite nor postgres in CI, so the behavior change introduced by this same PR (initializing unified storage at ResourceServer construction) is unverified on postgres; a postgres-specific startup regression would merge undetected.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Loss of CI regression coverage for the exact code path this PR changes.
raw_findings.impact: The only integration test exercising the storage-server module target now runs on neither sqlite nor postgres in CI, so the behavior change introduced by this same PR (initializing unified storage at ResourceServer construction) is unverified on postgres; a postgres-specific startup regression would merge undetected.
raw_findings.root_cause: The patch disables the failing test path rather than addressing why eager initialization breaks it under postgres in CI.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Diagnose and fix the postgres failure in CI (or gate on the actual failing condition) instead of skipping the whole test; at minimum file a tracked issue referenced in the TODO before merging.
raw_findings.title: Integration test silently skipped for postgres, removing coverage of the eager-init storage server path

raw_findings.body: Every startup failure emits the same error line twice, cluttering logs and making it look like two distinct failures occurred.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Duplicate identical error log lines on initialization failure degrade log signal quality.
raw_findings.impact: Every startup failure emits the same error line twice, cluttering logs and making it look like two distinct failures occurred.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new constructor-side error handling duplicates logging that already exists inside server.Init.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Remove the duplicate s.log.Error call in NewResourceServer and just return the error (or remove the one inside Init).
raw_findings.title: Init failure is logged twice with the identical message
raw_findings.trigger: Any initialization error: server.Init already logs 's.log.Error("error initializing resource server", "error", s.initErr)' inside the once.Do block before returning the error, and NewResourceServer now logs the same message again.

raw_findings.body: initWatcher and lifecycle.Init now run inside every NewResourceServer call: a backend whose watch setup errors turns a previously lazy per-request failure into a hard construction failure (potentially breaking Grafana startup for the dashboard legacy store), and every constructed server now spawns broadcaster/watch goroutines even if never used.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Startup failure or unnecessary background goroutines in embedding call sites that previously relied on lazy initialization.
raw_findings.impact: initWatcher and lifecycle.Init now run inside every NewResourceServer call: a backend whose watch setup errors turns a previously lazy per-request failure into a hard construction failure (potentially breaking Grafana startup for the dashboard legacy store), and every constructed server now spawns broadcaster/watch goroutines even if never used.
raw_findings.root_cause: Moving Init from first-request lazy invocation into the constructor applies eager watcher startup to all embedders, not just the standalone storage server the PR targets.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Audit all NewResourceServer call sites (the PR description itself asks this); either make eager init opt-in via ResourceServerOptions or verify each backend's WatchWriteEvents/lifecycle behaves safely at construction time.
raw_findings.title: Eager Init in constructor changes failure and resource semantics for all NewResourceServer callers
raw_findings.trigger: Callers that construct ResourceServer instances outside the gRPC storage server, e.g. DashboardStorage.NewStore (legacy Access backend), NewRESTOptionsGetterMemory/ForFile, and unified/client.go, whose backend's WatchWriteEvents may fail, block, or be unnecessary at construction time.
